claim: Piltdown Man was a genuine fossil of an early human ancestor.

heard.who: Scientists of the 1910s to 1940s who accepted the find, as described by PBS's A Science Odyssey
heard.quote: This "Piltdown Man" was believed by many to be "the earliest Englishman," and in fact, the missing link between apes and humans.

answer: No. Piltdown Man, presented in 1912 as the missing link between apes and humans, was shown in 1953 to be a forgery: a human skull with an orangutan's jaw. A 2016 re-analysis found that one forger made it, most likely the amateur collector Charles Dawson.

facts.text: In 1953 tests showed that Piltdown Man, presented in 1912 as the missing link between apes and humans, was a forgery: the skull was human and the jaw came from an orangutan.

sources.title: Piltdown Man
sources.quote: Their results showed that the skull and jaw fragments actually came from two different species, a human and an ape, probably an orangutan.

sources.title: Piltdown Man: Infamous Fake Fossil
sources.quote: In reality, the jawbones and tooth came from an orangutan and the skulls from medieval human bones, De Groote said.

sources.title: People and Discoveries: Piltdown Man is revealed as fake
sources.quote: But in 1953, the jawbone was found to be that of a modern ape -- orangutan, most likely -- that had been treated with chemicals to make it look as though it had been lying in the ground

facts.text: A 2016 re-analysis with DNA and CT scans found the Piltdown teeth came from a single orangutan and concluded the fake was the work of one forger, most likely Charles Dawson.

sources.title: Piltdown Man: Infamous Fake Fossil
sources.quote: determined that Dawson was the most likely sole forger.

sources.title: Piltdown Man: Anatomy of a Hoax
sources.quote: Their conclusion was that it was the work of a single hoaxer, using material from a single orangutan from Borneo

sources.title: How the Piltdown Man skull became the greatest hoax in anthropology
sources.quote: The most recent study in 2016 came to the conclusion that Charles Dawson probably acted alone.

contested.text: Who made the forgery. The 2016 study points to Dawson alone, but earlier accounts also named others, among them the Jesuit palaeontologist Teilhard de Chardin, the anatomist Arthur Keith and the writer Arthur Conan Doyle.

sources.title: Piltdown Man: Anatomy of a Hoax
sources.quote: the finger of suspicion also pointed at Teilhard de Chardin and Arthur Keith among others, as well as Sir Arthur Conan-Doyle, who lived nearby

could_not_verify: The 1953 Oakley, Weiner and Le Gros Clark paper itself; the museum page that summarises it was read instead.
Proof of who made the forgery; the 2016 study says 'most likely', and the sources describe it that way.
not_claimed: That every scientist of the time accepted the find; some doubted it early on.
